result.rationale: The minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts is a plain z.object that only declares access_token (plus a bogus computed key), so in sync mode Zod strips unknown fields like expiry_date from the parsed data. Office365CalendarService then merges `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`, so the stale expired expiry_date persists and triggers repeated refreshes — a real defect visible in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the minimumTokenResponseSchema uses z.object() which by default strips unknown fields. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, this schema is used instead of the app-specific schema. The minimumTokenResponseSchema only defines access_token and attempts to define dynamic keys (which is invalid Zod syntax - [z.string().toString()] doesn't work as intended). This means fields like 'expires_in' or 'expiry_date' from the actual token response would be stripped. In Office365CalendarService.ts, the code does 'o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }' - if expiry fields are stripped, the old expired timestamp remains, causing repeated refresh attempts. This is a real bug in the credential sync mode.
